module Positionable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  REBALANCE_THRESHOLD = 1e-10
  ELEMENT_GAP         = 1

  included do
    scope :positioned, -> { order(:position_score, :id) }

    scope :before, ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score < ?", other.position_score) }
    scope :after,  ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score > ?", other.position_score) }

    around_create :insert_at_default_position
    after_save_commit :rebalance_positions, if: :rebalance_required?
  end

  class_methods do
    def positioned_within(parent, association:, filter:)
      define_method :positioning_parent do
        send(parent)
      end

      define_method :all_positioned_siblings do
        positioning_parent.send(association).send(filter).positioned
      end

      define_method :other_positioned_siblings do
        all_positioned_siblings.excluding(self)
      end

      private :positioning_parent, :all_positioned_siblings, :other_positioned_siblings
    end
  end

  def previous
    other_positioned_siblings.before(self).last
  end

  def next
    other_positioned_siblings.after(self).first
  end

  def move_to_position(offset, followed_by: [])
    with_positioning_lock do
      all_to_move = [ self, *followed_by ]
      before, after = before_and_after_for(offset: offset, moving: all_to_move)
      gap = (after - before) / (all_to_move.count + 1)

      all_to_move.each.with_index(1) do |item, index|
        item.update!(position_score: before + (index * gap))
      end

      remember_to_rebalance_positions if gap < REBALANCE_THRESHOLD
    end
  end

  def position_as_percentage
    100 * ordinal_position.to_f / all_positioned_siblings.count
  end

  private
    def ordinal_position
      other_positioned_siblings.before(self).count + 1
    end

    def insert_at_default_position
      with_positioning_lock do
        position_at_end
        yield
      end
    end

    def position_at_start
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)) - ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def position_at_end
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score) || 0) + ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def before_and_after_for(offset:, moving:)
      other_items = all_positioned_siblings.excluding(moving)

      if offset < 1
        after = all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)
        before = after - ELEMENT_GAP
      else
        before, after = other_items.offset(offset - 1).limit(2).pluck(:position_score)
        before ||= all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score)
        after ||= before + (moving.count.succ * ELEMENT_GAP)
      end

      [ before, after ]
    end

    def remember_to_rebalance_positions
      @rebalance_required = true
    end

    def rebalance_required?
      @rebalance_required
    end

    def rebalance_positions
      with_positioning_lock do
        odered = all_positioned_siblings.select("row_number() over (order by position_score, id) as new_score, id")
        sql = "update #{self.class.table_name} set position_score = new_score from (#{odered.to_sql}) as ordered where #{self.class.table_name}.id = ordered.id"

        self.class.connection.execute sql
      end
      @rebalance_required = false
    end

    def with_positioning_lock(&block)
      positioning_parent.with_lock &block
    end

class Book::MaintenanceTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "compact_positions! preserves hand-arranged order and compacts gaps into 1..n" do
    leaves(:reading_picture).move_to_position(0)
    leaves(:welcome_section).move_to_position(3)
    leaves(:welcome_page).destroy!

    assert_equal expected_order, books(:handbook).leaves.positioned

    books(:handbook).compact_positions!

    assert_equal expected_order, books(:handbook).leaves.positioned.reload
    assert_equal [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ], books(:handbook).leaves.positioned.pluck(:position_score)
  end

  test "compact_positions! preserves relative position of trashed leaves when restored" do
    leaves(:welcome_section).move_to_position(3)
    leaves(:welcome_section).trashed!
    leaves(:summary_page).destroy!

    books(:handbook).compact_positions!
    leaves(:welcome_section).active!

    assert_equal [ leaves(:welcome_page), leaves(:reading_picture), leaves(:welcome_section) ],
      books(:handbook).leaves.active.positioned
  end

  test "compact_positions! breaks position_score ties by id" do
    leaves(:reading_picture).update!(position_score: 10)
    leaves(:welcome_section).update!(position_score: 10)
    leaves(:welcome_page).update!(position_score: 1)
    leaves(:summary_page).update!(position_score: 20)

    expected_order = books(:handbook).leaves.positioned.to_a

    books(:handbook).compact_positions!

    assert_equal expected_order, books(:handbook).leaves.positioned.reload
    assert_equal [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ], books(:handbook).leaves.positioned.pluck(:position_score)
  end

  test "compact_positions! only modifies leaves in the target book" do
    other_leaf = books(:manual).press Page.new(body: "Other"), title: "Other"
    other_leaf.update!(position_score: 42)

    books(:handbook).compact_positions!

    assert_equal 42, other_leaf.reload.position_score
  end

  test "live_leaf_count returns count of non-trashed leaves" do
    assert_equal 4, books(:handbook).live_leaf_count

    leaves(:summary_page).trashed!

    assert_equal 3, books(:handbook).live_leaf_count
    assert_equal 0, books(:manual).live_leaf_count
  end

  test "maintenance:compact_positions rake task compacts all books in positioned order" do
    leaves(:reading_picture).move_to_position(0)
    leaves(:welcome_page).destroy!
    expected_order = [ leaves(:reading_picture), leaves(:welcome_section), leaves(:summary_page) ]

    Rake::Task["maintenance:compact_positions"].reenable

    assert_equal [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ], books(:handbook).leaves.positioned.pluck(:position_score)
  end
end

Okay, here's my take on those commands, as though they were my own mental processes, targeted for an expert audience:

**Separate RuboCop and Test Runs: A Tactical Decision**

Right, let's break this down. The urge to run `bin/rubocop` (or `bundle exec rubocop`) and `bin/rails test` as separate commands is a subtle but important one. We're not just trying to execute code, we're strategizing our workflow.

Firstly, independent RuboCop runs offer granular control. By executing the linter before the test suite, we can catch style violations *before* they potentially snowball into test failures caused by, say, an unclosed `end` or inconsistent indentation (although frankly, with my setup, that's rare). It’s about preventative maintenance; cleaner code reduces cognitive load when debugging. This also offers a clean separation of concerns: code style first, functional correctness second. Plus, isolated RuboCop runs are faster because of the nature of the tasks involved.

Secondly, and perhaps more importantly for you, separating the test runs allows for quicker feedback loops. Running the tests independently after style fixes are applied enables a more precise identification of the source of any test failures that might arise after the style modifications. We want a clean test suite result to ensure the changes are correct and don't introduce regressions, which is critical during development. If a test fails after style changes, it is far more likely a logic error was introduced, rather than a style issue. This speeds up debugging.

In essence, these separate steps facilitate a more iterative and focused development process, optimizing both code quality and developer efficiency. We gain clarity, minimize noise, and maintain surgical precision with each iteration.
